repair_argument: For a strong map U take its simple approximation witness and Borel null N. Multiplying each simple map by 1_(Gamma minus N) preserves Borel simplicity; the modified maps converge at every point to U off N and 0 on N. The everywhere limit is a Borel V-valued map, since V is separable metric. Thus every class has a Borel version without changing the sigma-algebra.

Define scalar integrals through Borel versions. Two versions of one class agree outside a Borel null union. Their measurable nonnegative norm functions have equal nonnegative integrals, including infinite values; finite pairing integrals agree because the positive and negative parts of their difference vanish off that null union.

This preserves the original quotient: every newly permitted raw representative is almost everywhere equal to its Borel version, whose norm square was already measurable under the original definition. Conversely every originally admitted map is retained with the same norm integral and class. Only the allowed presentations and explicit integration convention are clarified; no quotient element is added or removed.

For affine forms, zero the simple approximants and raw maps on a common Borel exceptional null set. Partitionwise affine scalar functions are Borel and converge everywhere to the scalar forms of the Borel versions. Bounds by a*||U||||W|| and ||F||||W|| plus scalar Cauchy-Schwarz give integrability. Coercivity and continuity integrate with exactly a_* and a*. Different class representatives or versions yield integrands equal off a Borel null union, establishing independence.

The Hilbert proof must choose Borel versions before its pairing and norm-level-set arguments; the remaining completeness/density proof already performs the needed zeroing. The solution theorem must import version measurability precisely; its simple-test argument actually uses Borel pointwise functions.
